latest_release.body:
## 🌞 SO3LR v0.1.0 Release Notes

This release introduces a unified command-line interface, fine-tuning support, restart handling, stability and performance upgrades, and expanded documentation and examples.

### New Features

* **Unified CLI** for optimization (`opt`), MD (`nve`, `nvt`, `npt`), evaluation (`eval`), and fine-tuning (`finetune`).
* **Fine-tuning support** with multiple strategies and YAML settings.
* **Enhanced logging** with improved timing and progress reporting.
* **Seamless restarts** via `--restart-save` and `--restart-load`.
* **1.5× faster NPT** via the updated JAX-MD backend (jax-md/jax-md#330)

### Bug Fixes

* Numerous MD fixes, including box loading, NVE/NPT initialization, and thermostat/barostat behavior.
* Corrected force error metrics in `eval` (was overestimated ×3 for a few weeks).
* Various small naming, parsing, and formatting fixes.

### Documentation & Examples

* Updated README with a Colab example, dimer binding energy workflow, evaluation, and fine-tuning, and a roadmap.
* Clearer descriptions of units, defaults, and recommended cutoffs.

### What's Changed

* MD script, CLI restructuring, and README updates by @tohenkes — [https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/pull/16](https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/pull/16)
* CLI improvements by @kabylda — [https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/pull/18](https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/pull/18)
* NVE ensemble and restarts by @fbruenig — [https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/pull/20](https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/pull/20)
* Finetuning by @thorben-frank -  [https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/issues/3](https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/issues/3)
* NVE CLI fix by @PetraNavarcikova — [https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/pull/27](https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/pull/27)

### Contributors

Thanks to new contributors: **@tohenkes, @fbruenig, @PetraNavarcikova**, and everyone who helped improve stability, usability, and documentation.

**Full Changelog:** [https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/compare/v0.0.1...v0.1.0](https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/compare/v0.0.1...v0.1.0)

## About SO3LR - pronounced *Solar* - is a pretrained machine-learned force field for (bio)molecular simulations. It integrates the fast and stable SO3krates neural network for semi-local interactions with universal pairwise force fields designed for short-range repulsion, long-range electrostatics, and dispersion interactions. ## Installation Try SO3LR without any local installation using our [light web version](https://so3lr.github.io/gui/) or [Colab notebook](https://colab.research.google.com/github/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/blob/main/examples/so3lr_colab_example.ipynb). We recommend installing SO3LR with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (it's magical): ```shell git clone https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr.git cd so3lr uv sync --locked --extra cuda12 # GPU; drop --extra cuda12 for CPU source .venv/bin/activate so3lr --help ``` If JAX is already installed on your cluster (CUDA or ROCm), install SO3LR into that environment: ```shell git clone https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr.git cd so3lr uv pip install ".[cuda12]" # NVIDIA GPU; ROCm or CPU: uv pip install . so3lr --help ``` See the [installation guide](https://so3lr.github.io/installation/) for optional extras. More details about JAX installation can be found [here](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/installation.html). ## Quick start SO3LR provides a command-line interface for geometry optimization, molecular dynamics and evaluation. Each command can be run with `--help` to see all available options. ```shell # Geometry optimization so3lr opt --input geometry.xyz --force-conv 0.05 # NVT and NPT molecular dynamics so3lr nvt --input geometry.xyz --temperature 300 --dt 0.5 --md-cycles 100 --md-steps 100 so3lr npt --input geometry.xyz --temperature 300 --pressure 1.0 --dt 0.5 --md-cycles 100 --md-steps 100 # Evaluation on a dataset so3lr eval --datafile dataset.extxyz --lr-cutoff 100 --save-to predictions.extxyz ``` For longer simulations, use a settings file, `so3lr --settings settings.yaml` (see [molecular dynamics](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/md/)). To use SO3LR as an ASE calculator: ```python from ase.io import read from so3lr import So3lrCalculator atoms = read("geometry.xyz") atoms.info["charge"] = 0 # total charge; 0 if unset atoms.calc = So3lrCalculator(model="so3lr-tauri-m", lr_cutoff=100) energy = atoms.get_potential_energy() forces = atoms.get_forces() ``` Units are eV and Å. On the command line, periodic structures use PME for electrostatics and dispersion with a 10 Å real-space cutoff (2 Å smearing, 1.55 Å mesh), as in the paper's liquid and scaling simulations. The Python calculators default to 12 Å without k-space. For gas-phase simulations, we suggest using `--lr-cutoff 100`. ## Models The models are bundled with the package and selected by name. The SO3LR Tauri models cover H to At (Z = 1–85) and are described in the [SO3LR Tauri preprint](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2611.06237). - `so3lr-tauri-m` (default): start here; the model we use for biomolecular MD. - `so3lr-tauri-l`: the most accurate, recommended for reactions; 3.7× slower than `-m`. - `so3lr-tauri-s`: 1.4× faster than `-m`. - `so3lr`: the original model from the [JACS paper](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c09558), for H, C, N, O, F, P, S and Cl, kept to reproduce published results. Use the same name on the command line (`--model`) and in settings files (`model:`), or pass a path to a fine-tuned model. To pin a release for papers and benchmarks, add its date: `so3lr-tauri-m-2606`. ## Documentation The full documentation is at [so3lr.github.io](https://so3lr.github.io/), including: - [Command line](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/cli/) and [settings file](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/settings/) - [Molecular dynamics](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/md/) - [ASE calculator](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/ase/) and [dataset evaluation](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/evaluation/) - [Long-range electrostatics](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/electrostatics/) (Ewald, PME, P3M) - [Enhanced sampling](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/enhanced-sampling/) with PySAGES - [Observables](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/observables/), [gradients and Hessians](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/derivatives/) - [Binding energies](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/binding-energies/) - [Fine-tuning](https://so3lr.github.io/training/finetuning/) and [training from scratch](https://so3lr.github.io/training/from-scratch/) - [API reference](https://so3lr.github.io/reference/api/) and [FAQ](https://so3lr.github.io/reference/faq/) ## Datasets The quantum mechanical datasets used for training and testing SO3LR Tauri are available on Zenodo: [10.5281/zenodo.22920714](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22920714). The data for the legacy SO3LR model are at [10.5281/zenodo.14779793](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14779793). ## Contributing The code and models are still evolving, and your feedback is invaluable. We would appreciate if you [open an issue](https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/issues) for any errors, inconsistencies or feature ideas. See [`DEVELOPERS.md`](./DEVELOPERS.md) for development environments and tests. ## Citation If you use SO3LR, please cite the papers below: ```bibtex @article{kabylda2026so3lr, title = {{SO3LR Tauri: Generally Applicable Force Fields for Reactive (Bio)Molecular Simulations Covering the Periodic Table}}, author = {Kabylda, Adil and Br{\"{u}}nig, Florian N. and Gallegos, Miguel and Frank, J. Thorben and Moerman, Evgeny and Unke, Oliver T. and Chmiela, Stefan and M{\"{u}}ller, Klaus-Robert and Tkatchenko, Alexandre}, journal = {arXiv preprint arXiv:2611.06237}, year = {2026}, doi = {10.48550/arXiv.2611.06237}, url = {https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06237}, } @article{kabylda2025molecular, title={Molecular Simulations with a Pretrained Neural Network and Universal Pairwise Force Fields}, author={Kabylda, Adil and Frank, J Thorben and Su{\'a}rez-Dou, Sergio and Khabibrakhmanov, Almaz and Medrano Sandonas, Leonardo and Unke, Oliver T and Chmiela, Stefan and M{\"u}ller, Klaus-Robert and Tkatchenko, Alexandre}, journal={Journal of the American Chemical Society}, volume={147}, number={37}, pages={33723}, year={2025}, doi={10.1021/jacs.5c09558} } @article{frank2024euclidean, title={A Euclidean transformer for fast and stable machine learned force fields}, author={Frank, Thorben and Unke, Oliver and M{\"u}ller, Klaus-Robert and Chmiela, Stefan}, journal={Nature Communications}, volume={15}, number={1}, pages={6539}, year={2024}, doi={10.1038/s41467-024-50620-6} } ``` ## License The code and the legacy SO3LR model weights are released under the [MIT License](LICENSE), and the SO3LR Tauri weights under [CC BY-NC 4.0](licenses/LICENSE.CC-BY-NC-4.0).
